skills.name: character_body_kinematics
skills.skill: Implement robust kinematic controller pipelines for CharacterBody2D and CharacterBody3D with gravity, floor snapping, slope handling, and velocity integration.
procedure: Select CharacterBody2D or CharacterBody3D as root physics object with an appropriate CollisionShape child.
Declare velocity vectors and integrate standard project gravity using `get_gravity()` or `ProjectSettings.get_setting("physics/2d/default_gravity")` / `3d/default_gravity`.
Process player inputs in `_physics_process(delta)` using `Input.get_axis()` or `Input.get_vector()` into normalized move directions.
Apply directional acceleration and friction towards target velocity using `Vector2.move_toward()` or `Vector3.move_toward()`.
Execute `move_and_slide()` to resolve collisions against static, animatable, and rigid bodies.
Configure `floor_snap_length`, `floor_max_angle`, and `floor_stop_on_slope` properties to prevent airborne jitter on declivities.
verification: Verify `is_on_floor()` returns true when stationary on walkable surfaces.
Check that vertical velocity does not compound infinitely while grounded.
Run simulation over sloped geometry up to configured `floor_max_angle` to ensure no downward bouncing.
pitfalls: Multiplying velocity by delta before calling `move_and_slide()`; in Godot 4, delta is automatically applied internally.
Modifying global position directly instead of assigning to `velocity` prior to `move_and_slide()`.
Omitting collision shape assignments, causing silent collision bypass.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Create a CharacterBody3D player script in Godot 4.7.2 featuring 8-direction WASD movement, jumping with proper gravity integration, acceleration/deceleration damping, and stable slope traversal using move_and_slide().

skills.name: animation_tree_state_machine
skills.skill: Configure and control AnimationTree with AnimationNodeStateMachine and AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D for responsive character locomotion blending.
procedure: Attach an AnimationPlayer to the node hierarchy containing required clips (idle, walk, run, jump).
Attach an AnimationTree, set `anim_player` path to target AnimationPlayer, and set `tree_root` to `AnimationNodeStateMachine`.
Add nodes within the state machine: combine locomotion clips into an `AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D` and discrete actions into independent `AnimationNodeAnimation` or `AnimationNodeOneShot` nodes.
Construct `AnimationNodeStateMachineTransition` edges between states, configuring cross-fade times and auto-advance rules.
Activate the tree by setting `active = true`.
Query the playback controller via `var playback = animation_tree["parameters/playback"] as AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback`.
Update blend space parameters via `animation_tree.set("parameters/Locomotion/blend_position", input_dir)` in `_process` or `_physics_process`.
verification: Verify state transitions occur without hitching by asserting `playback.get_current_node()` matches expectations during simulated input.
Check that blend coordinates smoothly interpolate between idle and movement animations.
pitfalls: Using legacy `AnimationTreePlayer` patterns instead of Godot 4's parameter path notation `parameters/<NodeName>/<Property>`.
Calling `travel()` on a null playback reference due to unassigned or inactive `AnimationTree`.
Setting `advance_mode` to `ADVANCE_MODE_AUTO` without a valid switch condition, causing instant unwanted state transitions.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Set up a script and node structure connecting an AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer. Implement state transitions between Idle, Locomotion (using BlendSpace2D for directional run/walk), and an Attack one-shot animation triggered via an exported trigger method.

skills.name: audio_stream_polyphony_management
skills.skill: Manage dynamic, low-latency concurrent sound effects using AudioStreamPolyphonic and AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic inside AudioStreamPlayer nodes.
procedure: Instantiate an `AudioStreamPlayer`, `AudioStreamPlayer2D`, or `AudioStreamPlayer3D` node.
Assign an `AudioStreamPolyphonic` resource to its `stream` property and set `polyphony` limit (e.g., 16-32 channels).
Play the player node via `play()` to initialize the underlying playback buffer.
Retrieve the polyphonic stream playback via `var playback = player.get_stream_playback() as AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic`.
Trigger sound instances using `var voice_id = playback.play_stream(sample_resource, from_offset, volume_db, pitch_scale)`.
Manage active voices using `playback.is_stream_playing(voice_id)` and adjust volumes or stop voices dynamically using `playback.stop_stream(voice_id)`.
verification: Verify `playback != null` and is an instance of `AudioStreamPlaybackPolyphonic`.
Test concurrent audio playback triggers up to polyphony capacity without audio dropouts or node allocation overhead.
Confirm voice IDs return false on `is_stream_playing(id)` after sound duration expires.
pitfalls: Attempting to call `get_stream_playback()` before calling `play()` on the AudioStreamPlayer, returning null.
Instantiating dozens of individual `AudioStreamPlayer` nodes for rapid sound effects instead of using a single polyphonic stream, causing scene tree overhead.
Exceeding the pre-allocated polyphony stream count, causing silent voice drops.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Construct a GDScript sound manager that uses an AudioStreamPlayer configured with AudioStreamPolyphonic to play overlapping sound effects with randomized pitch modulation and volume scaling without instantiating extra player nodes.

skills.name: astar2d_grid_pathfinding
skills.skill: Build grid-based pathfinding systems utilizing AStarGrid2D with obstacle avoidance, region bounding, and cell weight configuration.
procedure: Instantiate an `AStarGrid2D` instance in script.
Define grid boundaries via `region = Rect2i(start_pos, size_in_cells)` and `cell_size = Vector2(cell_w, cell_h)`.
Set `diagonal_mode` (e.g., `DIAGONAL_MODE_NEVER`, `DIAGONAL_MODE_AT_LEAST_ONE_WALKABLE`, or `DIAGONAL_MODE_ALWAYS`).
Set `heuristic` using `HEURISTIC_MANHATTAN`, `HEURISTIC_EUCLIDEAN`, or `HEURISTIC_OCTILE`.
Invoke `update()` to allocate the internal grid structures.
Synchronize static obstacles from TileMapLayer or collision objects by setting `set_point_solid(cell_coords, true)`.
Query paths at runtime using `get_point_path(from_cell, to_cell)` or `get_id_path(from_cell, to_cell)`.
verification: Verify `is_in_bounds(x, y)` returns true for valid navigation requests.
Assert `get_point_path()` returns an empty array when destination is blocked or unreachable.
Check that solid coordinates are bypassed correctly in generated point sequences.
pitfalls: Forgetting to call `astar_grid.update()` after configuring region, cell size, or diagonal mode, resulting in invalid path calculations.
Passing world-space pixel coordinates directly into `set_point_solid` or `get_id_path` instead of cell-index coordinates.
Overlooking diagonal corner clipping where entities cut through solid diagonals; mitigate using `DIAGONAL_MODE_AT_LEAST_ONE_WALKABLE`.
skills.benchmark_prompt: Write a pathfinding manager using AStarGrid2D that initializes a 100x100 grid, marks arbitrary rectangular zones as obstacles, and exposes a function `get_world_route(start: Vector2, end: Vector2) -> PackedVector2Array` converting world coordinates to grid queries and back.
